cim_eredeti: Anthropic's IPO Raised $81 Billion. Here’s Which Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks Will Benefit From Where the Money Goes.
szoveg_eredeti:
By Jennifer Saibil – Nov 24, 2026 at 12:23PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›

Anthropic (ANT -10.71%) made history last week as the largest initial public offering (IPO) ever, raising $81 billion.

Companies that go public do so to raise money for specific purposes — usually to fund growth. Anthropic's stated goals for the money it raised were similar to the usual, with an artificial intelligence (AI) twist: Beyond covering its needs for working capital, it plans to lease compute and build infrastructure.

If you're bullish on AI but not ready to invest in a young, unprofitable company that has just gone public, you can get exposure to Anthropic’s growth potential by investing in the companies that are set to benefit from the data center build-out it will require. Here are some of them.

Anthropic has a five-year deal with Broadcom (AVGO -3.74%) for custom AI accelerators worth $161.2 billion. Alphabet (GOOG -1.14%)(GOOGL -1.27%) is included as well because the chips in question are its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), which Broadcom designs, and Alphabet will lease them to Anthropic. TPUs aren't as versatile as graphics processing units (GPUs), but they don't have to be. They are application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) that are constructed for a much narrower range of workloads, but because of that, they offer a cheaper solution for what they do well.

In September, Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said that his company expects Anthropic to become its largest custom-chip customer in 2027, and that Broadcom has line of sight to sales of 19 gigawatts of power, in collaboration with Alphabet. He also said that Anthropic would remain its top customer in 2028. On top of that, following a similar model to the one Nvidia (NVDA -7.17%) has repeatedly used — and which has been described as “circular financing” — Broadcom has loaned Anthropic $42 billion via a purchase of convertible notes.

Alphabet has a $40 billion equity stake in Anthropic, and it also has a partnership with the company that buys its compute power. It may have commitments as high as $200 billion, according to reports.

It's not just Google. Anthropic has agreements with multiple companies for compute power, including Amazon (AMZN -0.78%), with which it has commitments for $110 billion in compute capacity. These deals are in place through 2036, and they commit Anthropic to paying for that capacity no matter how much of it the AI lab ends up needing.

Anthropic uses Amazon's Tranium chips — another type of ASIC — and the two companies have had a deal for years. Amazon was one of the earliest investors in Anthropic and has partnered with it since its beginnings. It announced a $4 billion investment in Anthropic in 2024 and has since added to that stake multiple times.

In April of this year, Amazon committed another $5 billion to the company at the same time it secured a $5 billion commitment from it, and it pledged another $20 billion "in the future."

Anthropic also has compute deals with Microsoft (MSFT +1.37%) for at least $47.2 billion and up to $49.2 billion through 2033. It's also committed regardless of usage and is uncancelable. Anthropic’s AI models are available to customers through many Microsoft products, and Microsoft has invested $5 billion in the company.

Anthropic has a massive deal with Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -5.05%), aka SpaceX, for data center capacity provided by Nvidia chips. It's committed to spending $120.5 billion through 2029 to rent compute capacity from SpaceX's massive Colossus data center clusters, with a full rentout of Colossus I, which has 220,000 Nvidia processors. That provides it with 300 megawatts of compute power monthly.

The AI trade is in flux right now, with Nvidia stock down 12% this year and Anthropic stock off to a rough start. Although all the companies on this list should benefit from these deals, there may be continued volatility in the near future, and investors should keep that in mind when considering which AI stocks to buy right now.
